children: The partnerships span semiconductor materials, fab engineering, chip packaging, and supply-chain infrastructure as Tata Electronics builds out its manufacturing ecosystem

Tata Electronics on Friday signed multiple Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and announced partnerships with global companies at Semicon India 2026, as it expands the ecosystem around its upcoming semiconductor manufacturing and packaging facilities in Gujarat and Assam.

Tata Electronics CEO and Managing Director Randhir Thakur said, “The question of whether we can make chips in India has changed to how fast and how deep can we build the semiconductor ecosystem in India.”

The agreements will strengthen different parts of the semiconductor value chain, with partnerships spanning semiconductor materials, engineering capabilities, packaging technologies and supply-chain infrastructure across the company’s planned facilities.
Localising Chip Materials

Tata Electronics signed an MoU with Japan's Sumitomo Chemical to explore the supply and local manufacture of semiconductor materials and high-purity chemicals for its upcoming semiconductor fab in Dholera, Gujarat.

Under the partnership, Sumitomo Chemical will explore supplying semiconductor materials including photoresists, functional chemicals and high-purity chemicals such as hydrogen peroxide, isopropyl alcohol, ammonia water and sulphuric acid to Tata Electronics' Dholera fab.

The companies will also explore local manufacturing of Sumitomo Chemical's semiconductor materials and high-purity chemicals in India. Tata Electronics said the collaboration will strengthen supply-chain diversification and improve the availability of high-quality materials for semiconductor manufacturing.

Tata Electronics is building a 12-inch (300 mm) commercial semiconductor fab in Dholera with a planned investment of USB 11 billion. The facility will manufacture chips for applications including automotive, mobile devices, and artificial intelligence.
Accelerating Fab Readiness

Tata Electronics also announced a collaboration with Malaysian integrated engineering solutions provider Kelington to support the deployment of critical infrastructure and systems required for semiconductor manufacturing at the Dholera facility.

The partnership intends to accelerate the fab's operational readiness for silicon wafer production. It will also explore the development of local talent and advanced design-and-build engineering capabilities in India.

Thakur said tool hook-up is a critical element in establishing a reliable and efficient fab environment, enabling the integration of sophisticated equipment and supporting operational excellence from day one.
Strengthening Chip Packaging
Separately, Tata Electronics signed an MoU with Japanese precision semiconductor component manufacturer Enomoto to support its semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam.
Enomoto will leverage its research and development capabilities, technical know-how and next-generation solutions to accelerate semiconductor packaging readiness at the facility.
The companies will also explore localising lead-frame manufacturing in India, along with opportunities for technology transfer, engineering collaboration and capability development.
Tata Electronics is developing an indigenous high-volume semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad with an investment of USD 3 billion.
Building Materials Logistics
Tata Electronics also partnered with Japan's Sojitz Corporation and NRS Corporation to establish a framework for the supply and storage of critical semiconductor materials for the Dholera fab.

Under the partnership, Sojitz and NRS will explore and validate a supply-chain management framework covering the safe, reliable and efficient handling of semiconductor materials, including materials requiring specialised handling.

The companies are also engaging with Dholera Industrial City Development Limited to secure a suitable site within the Dholera Special Investment Region and are assessing the permits, licences and regulatory frameworks required for the import, transportation, storage, handling and management of semiconductor materials.

Thakur said the partners' expertise in semiconductor chemicals, hazardous-material handling and warehouse operations would support Tata Electronics' operational readiness and its goal of building a resilient supply chain for global customers.
Tata Electronics also signed a separate MoU with Larsen & Toubro (L&T) on Friday.
